description.narrative: The Multi-Donor Trust Fund, through which Ireland channels funding to the SDG PF, is a payment for results mechanism based on twenty Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs) that have been agreed with the Ministry of Health (MoH) and are aligned with the Health Sector Medium Term Development and Investment Plan (HSDIP) priorities. The SDG PF, a multi-donor pooled fund mechanism, finances underfunded priority areas within the Government of Ethiopia’s HSDIP. The HSDIP (2023-2026) overall goal is to improve the health status of the population through accelerating progress towards Universal Health Care (UHC). Within the SDG-PF's broad scope of strengthening universal healthcare, Ireland's contribution is focued on maternal and child health - we support specific disbursement-linked indicator areas - increasing the number of deliveries attended by skilled providers, enhancing access to modern contraception, expanding youth-friendly health services (particularly for young women). In addition, Ireland supports the national health adaptation plan to climate change within SDG-PF (in line with our committment to climate-proofing all programmes we support). This is funded from within our budget’s Output 4: 'Gender equality is advanced through women and girls realising their rights, living healthier lives and accessing productive resources'. Three of the four ‘indicator areas’ we support are specifically on women’s health (with a fourth on climate, in line with our climate-proofing commitments).
